core_obligations: Choose a representative of an arbitrary class in H^1(R; G) as an element t of a maximal torus T(C) of G(C) satisfying t t^sigma = 1, and arrange by weak approximation for the variety of maximal tori that T is defined over Q (source lines 252-255).

Form the torus R = Res_{L/Q} T and exhibit the isomorphism phi from T(C) to R(R) with phi(T(L)) = R(Q), together with the Q-automorphism tau of R characterised by phi(x^sigma) = phi(x)^tau, and verify that the set of r in R with r r^tau = 1 is a subtorus by transporting it along an L-isomorphism psi from R to T x T that sends R(R) to the pairs (x, x^sigma) (source lines 257-270).

Show that the norm-one subtorus is defined over Q and that its rational points are dense in its real points by weak approximation at the infinite place, and pick a rational point q of it in the same connected component of the real points as phi(t) (source lines 272-276).

Conclude that q' = phi^{-1}(q) lies in T(L) and represents the same class in H^1(R; G) as t, because the two lie in the same connected component of the set of w in T(R) with w w^sigma = 1, so that the class of t lies in the image of the restriction map from H^1(L/F; G(L)) (source lines 277-281).

proof_roadmap.step: Represent a real cohomology class by an element of a Q-defined maximal torus with t t^sigma = 1.
Pass to the restriction of scalars and identify the norm-one subtorus through the isomorphism R = T x T.
Use weak approximation at the infinite place to find a rational point in the right connected component.
Conclude that the class comes from H^1 of the imaginary quadratic extension.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the lemma at source lines 245-249, label KneserHasse: for a connected semisimple algebraic group G over the rationals and any imaginary quadratic extension L, the natural restriction map from H^1(L/Q; G(L)) to H^1(R; G) is surjective. The proof retained at source lines 251-282 is the author's own argument rather than a citation: it represents an arbitrary real cohomology class by an element t of a maximal torus with t t^sigma = 1 and uses weak approximation for the variety of maximal tori to make that torus rational, then passes to the restriction of scalars R = Res_{L/Q} T, exhibits the L-isomorphism R = T x T that turns the norm-one condition r r^tau = 1 into an explicitly described subtorus, proves that this subtorus is defined over Q, and finishes by moving the class along a rational point produced by weak approximation at the infinite place. The non-routine content is exactly this combination: the cohomological representative has to be replaced by a rational point lying in the same connected component of a norm-one torus, which needs both the explicit model of the restriction of scalars and the archimedean density statement. Neither surjectivity nor the existence of such a representative follows from the definitions of Galois cohomology or from formal Hasse-principle arguments alone.
